channel.title: openv6 blog
channel.description: Guides on IPv6 proxies, anti-detect browsers and self-hosted static proxies.

item.title: Why Some Websites Won't Open Through an IPv6 Proxy (and Fixes That Don't Leak IPv4)
item.description: A site fails through your IPv6 proxy. Is it DNS hiding the IPv6 record, an IPv4-only site, or a site refusing your range? How to tell, and fixes that keep your real IPv4 hidden.

item.title: Match Time Zone, Language and Geolocation to Your Proxy in Anti-Detect Browsers
item.description: A profile whose time zone or language disagrees with its proxy IP stands out. Which settings to match, where to find the right values, and how to fill them for many profiles at once.

item.title: Anti-Detect Browser Says “Proxy Check Failed”? Causes and Fixes
item.description: The proxy works in one anti-detect browser and fails the check in another. Where the check really runs, the usual causes (scope, credentials, format, IPv4-only check services) and how to find which one.

item.title: What Is an IPv6 Proxy? A Plain-English Guide for Multi-Account Work
item.description: An IPv6 proxy sends your traffic out from an IPv6 address instead of IPv4. Here is how IPv6 proxies work, why one fixed IPv6 per account matters, and when they beat IPv4 proxies.

item.title: How to Turn Your Home Internet Into Static IPv6 Proxies
item.description: Step-by-step: turn the IPv6 /64 your home ISP already gives you into dozens or hundreds of fixed HTTP/SOCKS5 proxies with residential addresses, using a Windows, macOS or Linux machine.

item.title: Proxy Setup for Anti-Detect Browsers: Multilogin, GoLogin, Dolphin Anty, AdsPower, ixBrowser
item.description: Which proxy format each anti-detect browser expects, HTTP vs SOCKS5, remote DNS, and the rules that keep profiles separate: one fixed proxy per profile, no IPv4 fallback, matching time zones.

item.title: IPv6 Proxies on a VPS: Turn One /64 (or a /48) Into Hundreds of Proxies
item.description: How to run your own static IPv6 proxies on a cheap VPS: on-link /64 vs routed /56 and /48 prefixes, one /64 per proxy, firewall ports, and managing several servers from one dashboard.

item.title: Does My ISP Support IPv6? How to Check on Windows, macOS and Linux
item.description: Find out in two minutes whether your internet connection has IPv6 and a /64 prefix, using built-in commands on Windows, macOS and Linux, plus what to do if it doesn't.

item.title: /64 vs /56 vs /48: How IPv6 Prefixes Affect Account Separation
item.description: Why platforms treat an IPv6 /64 like one household, how many /64 networks a /56 or /48 contains, and how to give every account its own /64 with proxies.

item.title: Self-Hosted IPv6 Proxies vs Rented Proxies: Cost, Control and Trade-offs
item.description: Residential, ISP, datacenter and self-hosted IPv6 proxies compared: how each is billed, how stable the IPs are, which sites they reach, and when running your own proxies pays off.
